text:
maria: Seeing 4-node TP runs hang around step ~2400 after yesterday's kernel-selector tweak. Root log shows: `ncclAllReduce failed: unhandled cuda error`. Happening ~10% of runs. Anyone seen this?

sam: Can you paste the error block + which commit?

maria: pastebin of small snippet but here's the tail: ```
[2403] rank 2: calling ncclAllReduce(...)
E NCCL failure 2: Unhandled cuda error
Traceback (most recent call last):
  at runtime/comm/allreduce.cu:line 412
  at runtime/runtime.cc:line 1203
```

devon: Quick suspicion: kvcache invalidation race during TP reshard/rollout. We saw similar hang once when invalidation wasn't synchronized across ranks.

jia: I profiled the busy run — NVTX shows allreduce queued on rank 1 but never scheduled, while rank 0 is stuck trying to apply a kvcache delta. Attaching short flame (small): `cpu: 38% apply_delta -> mutex wait; gpu: waiting in ncclSchedule`

aanand: Did the kernel-selector change touch any codepaths that touch KV cache commit or rendezvous ordering?

maria: kernel-selector change is only choosing different matmul kernels + changed op fusion ordering. But the change bumped a couple of op schedules earlier in the graph which could reorder when we flush pending kvcache writes. commit: 9f3b2d7 (deploy-bot shows it went out at 2026-11-06 02:12 UTC)

deploy-bot: Deployed service/runtime@9f3b2d7 to canary (eng-runtime) — 02:12 UTC — health: green

sam: Can you reproduce w/ disabled kernel-selector? If it goes away, great narrow.

maria: I ran 12 attempts on canary w/ kernel-selector reverted — 12/12 succeed. With 9f3b2d7 on canary: 3/20 hang. So pretty correlated.

devon: Repro steps I used: `./run_tp_repro.sh --nodes 4 --tp 2 --seed 7 --warmup 50 --steps 3000`
Also added additional logging to kvcache apply path: `KVCACHE: rank=%d apply start seq=%d` and `apply end`.

jia: Look at rendezvous ordering: when reshard happens we do `lock(kv)->apply->release->signal`. If a different kernel schedule delays release on one rank it can leave others waiting at NCCL barrier/AllReduce expecting the tensor layout. We should add a simple explicit barrier after kvcache apply during reshard to be safe.

aanand: +1 for barrier guard as short-term mitigation. Long term we should ensure kernel-selector doesn't reorder observable op side-effects.

sam: Side-effect note: adding a full NCCL barrier will increase latency on cold reshard paths but this is rare and preferable to hangs. Could gate behind a flag: `--kvcache-sync-barrier` default on for multi-node.

maria: I pushed a tiny canary patch to serialize kvcache apply -> call `comm.barrier()` in reshard path: branch `kvcache/serialize-apply`. Ran 30 attempts on canary -> 30/30 success. Logs show `KVCACHE: rank=0 apply end` across ranks within ~12ms.

devon: Nice. Also add a test that injects a delay in kernel selector to mimic the reorder so we don't regress.

jia: I'll add a unit/integration test: `test_kvcache_sync_during_reshard` that runs 2-node and 4-node scenarios and flips a `SKIP_KV_BARRIER` env to test both.

sam: We should also backfill an assertion in the rendezvous code to check sequence numbers match before entering allreduce and alert + fail fast otherwise.

aanand: Agree. Filed issue #4127: "kvcache: guard reshard ordering + assert seq before allreduce" and assigned to devon+jia.

maria: Plan: merge `kvcache/serialize-apply` to canary today, monitor for 24h, then promote to prod if green. Add regression tests to CI.

devon: FYI I also collected NCCL debug from a failing run: attached `NCCL INFO` lines show `collOp` scheduled on subset then deadlock; will upload to infra for NVLink/sched debugging.

maria: Thanks all — big help. I'll own the canary and post metrics. Ping me if you want to join the watch. :thumbsup:

sam: tldr; root cause likely kvcache apply + kernel-selector reorder -> unsynchronized state across ranks -> nccl hang. Short term: barrier; long term: stricter op ordering guarantees + tests.

deploy-bot: Canary patch merged to canary at 1848765478 by maria — CI green.

maria: scheduling watch window 12:00-16:00 PT tomorrow, adding oncall rotation.

devon: reopening if we see any spike.

jia: I'll follow up with PR for tests and the rendezvous seq assert.

maria: closing thread for now, will re-open if we see regressions. Thanks everyone.
